title: Bushy chorion, smooth chorion and the deciduae

objective.text: Describe how the chorion and the uterine lining change by month 3 to set up the placenta and membranes.

body.general: Finger-like villi first cover the whole outer sac, the chorion [f1]. Near the embryo they keep growing: the bushy chorion frondosum [f2]. Elsewhere they fade, leaving the smooth chorion laeve by month 3 [f3]. The uterine lining, the decidua, has three parts [f4,f5,f6]. The decidua basalis, under the frondosum, forms the placenta with it [f5,f8]. The decidua capsularis covers the far side; the decidua parietalis lines the rest [f6]. Later the chorion laeve fuses with the parietalis, closing the uterine cavity [f7]. The amnion (inner sac) and chorion fuse as the amniochorionic membrane, which breaks in labour [f9,f10].
body.mbbs: Early on, villi cover the entire chorion [f1]. Villi at the embryonic pole keep growing and branching as the chorion frondosum [f2]. Those at the abembryonic pole degenerate, so by month 3 that side is the smooth chorion laeve [f3]. The decidua is the functional layer of the endometrium, shed at parturition [f4]. Over the frondosum lies the decidua basalis [f5]. Its compact layer of large, lipid- and glycogen-rich decidual cells, the decidual plate, is firmly bound to the chorion [f5,f11]. Over the abembryonic pole lies the decidua capsularis; the rest is the decidua parietalis [f6]. As the sac grows, the capsularis stretches and degenerates [f7]. The chorion laeve then fuses with the decidua parietalis, obliterating the uterine cavity [f7]. Only the frondosum takes part in exchange; with the decidua basalis it forms the placenta [f8]. Amnion and chorion fuse as the amniochorionic membrane, obliterating the chorionic cavity [f9].

facts.text: Early in development, villi cover the whole surface of the chorion.
Villi at the embryonic pole keep growing and branching; this part is the chorion frondosum, the bushy chorion.
Villi at the opposite, abembryonic pole degenerate, so by month 3 that side is smooth: the chorion laeve.
The decidua is the functional layer of the uterine lining, which is shed at birth.
The decidua over the chorion frondosum is the decidua basalis; its compact layer, the decidual plate, is tightly bound to the chorion.
The decidua over the abembryonic pole is the decidua capsularis; the rest of the uterine lining is the decidua parietalis.
As the chorionic sac grows, the decidua capsularis stretches and degenerates, and the chorion laeve fuses with the decidua parietalis, closing off the uterine cavity.
Only the chorion frondosum takes part in exchange; together with the decidua basalis it forms the placenta.
The amnion fuses with the chorion to form the amniochorionic membrane, which closes off the chorionic cavity.
The amniochorionic membrane is the membrane that ruptures in labour, when the waters break.
The decidual plate is made of large decidual cells rich in lipid and glycogen.

misconceptions.right: It has a fetal part, the chorion frondosum, and a maternal part, the decidua basalis.

checks.prompt: Which tissues together make the placenta?
checks.why: The placenta has a fetal part (chorion frondosum) and a maternal part (the decidua basalis beneath it).

checks.prompt: Put these changes in the chorion in order.
options: Villi (finger-like tufts) cover the whole chorion
The far (abembryonic) side turns smooth, the chorion laeve
The uterine cavity is closed off
checks.why: The far-side villi are lost first; only later, as the sac grows, does the smooth chorion meet and fuse with the opposite uterine wall.

checks.prompt: Early on, which part of the decidua covers the chorion laeve on the side facing the uterine cavity?
checks.why: The capsularis covers the far side; the basalis lies under the bushy chorion and the parietalis lines the rest of the uterus.

adult: This becomes the placenta, chorion frondosum plus decidua basalis [f8], and the membrane that breaks in labour [f10].

remember.a: The bushy chorion next to the embryo, where its finger-like villi keep growing [f2].

remember.q: Which decidua lies under the bushy chorion?
remember.a: The decidua basalis; with the bushy chorion it forms the placenta [f5,f8].

remember.q: Which membrane breaks when the waters break?
remember.a: The amniochorionic membrane: the amnion (the inner fluid sac) fused to the chorion [f9,f10].
